mission.title: qdrant: Allow Qdrant to run on read-only FS
mission.description: Allow Qdrant to run on read-only FS. Community-requested feature.

steps.title: Check current qdrant deployment
steps.description:
Verify your qdrant version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n qdrant -l app.kubernetes.io/name=qdrant
helm list -n qdrant 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working qdrant installation.

steps.title: Review qdrant configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant qdrant configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n qdrant -l app.kubernetes.io/name=qdrant
kubectl get configmap -n qdrant -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=qdrant
```
Currently qdrant requires write access to storage directory, even if there are no write operations happening in the system.
It would be interesting in some scenarios to have an ability to run qdrant from read-only FS.

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n qdrant -l app.kubernetes.io/name=qdrant
kubectl get events -n qdrant --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "Allow Qdrant to run on read-only FS" is functioning correctly.

resolution.summary:
### Proposed Solution

**Analysis:**
The root cause of the issue is that Qdrant requires write access to the storage directory, even when there are no write operations happening in the system. This is a limitation in scenarios where Qdrant needs to run from a read-only file system, such as a mounted network file system.
